what_this_is: Executable falsifications. Each arm names a gate, a mutation to a tracked file, and the command that must go RED. `scripts/check_gate_registry.py --demonstrate` applies the mutation to the real tree, runs the real gate, requires a non-zero exit AND the recorded diagnostic, then restores the file from git. A demonstration in this repo is a thing that RUNS, not a sentence in a header that was true once.
rules: An arm refuses to run if its target file is already dirty; it restores from git and will not clobber an edit.
An arm that finds the UNMUTATED gate already red is a FAILURE, not a pass: a red arm on a red tree proves nothing.
A mutation whose pattern does not match is a FAILURE, not a skip. That silent no-op is instance 4 (four perturbation batteries, vacuous because a failed substitution never aborted).
expect_contains pins WHY it went red. A gate that exits non-zero for an unrelated reason has not been demonstrated.

kernel_soundness_gate.arm: the differential corpus is edited without re-minting the baseline
kernel_soundness_gate.why: MEASURED 2026-08-27: the gate pins its own corpus by digest, so a silently-edited differential input is refused before any lane can pass on it. Recorded because this row was pinned but had NO arms. THIS ARM COULD NOT RUN AT ALL UNTIL 2026-08-27: its `append` mutation carried the key `content`, and `_apply` reads `mut["text"]`, so `--demonstrate kernel_soundness_gate` died with `KeyError: 'text'` after the green baseline run and before planting anything. The registry called it `replayable: true` and R5 EVIDENCE never noticed, because R5 only checks that the record MENTIONS the gate -- it does not validate the mutation's op schema. Fixed here (`content` -> `text`) and REPLAYED; three more arms in this file are still un-runnable for the same class of reason and are recorded in docs/analysis/2026-08-27-trust-core-gates-wired-and-wired-by-disposition.md section 5, because fixing an arm one cannot replay is not an improvement. THE EVIDENCE REDIRECT IS ALSO PART OF THE ARM, added 2026-08-27 after this demonstrator was measured leaving a FAILED-RUN artifact in the tree: `--demonstrate` restores the file it MUTATED, but this gate also MINTS reports/kernel-soundness-launch-evidence.json and nothing restored that -- so the committed artifact read `"status": "failed"` with expression_count 2002, the arm's own fingerprint, while the gate was green at HEAD on the real 2001-expression corpus. KERNEL_SOUNDNESS_EVIDENCE_PATH sends both the baseline mint and the mutated mint to a temp file. Nothing about the arm is weakened: the gate's verdict is its exit status and its per-lane lines, both produced before the artifact is written. RE-RUN planted-observed-reverted after the change, and it still fires -- see the replay line recorded in docs/analysis/2026-08-27-trust-core-gates-wired-and-wired-by-disposition.md section 5. The identical one-word fix is owed to the deny_sorry_gate arm and is deliberately NOT applied there: that arm's mutation target was dirty from a concurrent lane, --demonstrate correctly refuses to clobber it, and an unreplayed edit to a demonstration record is exactly the artifact this registry exists to stop shipping. The general fix is for --demonstrate to restore what a gate MINTS, not only what it MUTATES.

prelude-axiom-ratchet.arm: the census stops naming an axiom the default `clean check` prelude really asserts
prelude-axiom-ratchet.why: Dropping Fact.out from the pinned list is the same event, in reverse, as an init_* function ADDING an axiom: the live set stops being a subset of the pinned one. The gate names the offender rather than only moving a counter, which is why expect_contains can pin the axiom itself. Deliberately NOT a counter bump -- baseline_debt_proposition stays 2, so this arm exercises refusal 1 (the by-name subset check) in isolation rather than refusal 2. RETARGETED 2026-08-27 (#49): the arm used to drop Nat.lt_succ_iff, but that axiom is now a kernel-checked theorem (nat_lt_succ_iff_proof.rs), and dropping a name the prelude no longer asserts would be VACUOUS -- the pinned set would merely become a superset of the live one and refusal 1 would not fire at all. Fact.out is one of the two asserted propositions the default prelude still ships. The ratchet is read at RUNTIME, so the arm costs no clean-kernel recompile once the test binary exists; both the unmutated baseline and the mutated run are ~80 s of test. TWO FURTHER ARMS NEED NO MUTATION AT ALL and run in this same command: prelude_axiom_ratchet_refuses_a_theorem_that_wraps_a_prelude_axiom (a kernel-ACCEPTED `Declaration::Theorem` whose value IS `Fact.out` -- CLAUDE.md's 'wrapping an Axiom is NOT a proof' shape -- must be flagged by the real theorem_debt_problems predicate; it asserts its target is still an axiom, so it fails LOUDLY rather than going vacuous when that target is drained, which is exactly how the #49 retirement was caught) and prelude_axiom_ratchet_refuses_a_newly_planted_axiom (`axiom _ : True` must land in debt_proposition, `axiom _ : Prop` in debt_signature, and new_axiom_problems must fire on both the by-name check and the count).

rust_frontend.arm: a tracked source file drifts from the PINNED formatter and the driver must name it
rust_frontend.why: AUTHORED 2026-08-27 because this row had NO ARMS AT ALL while carrying a `demonstrated` sha -- so it could never be re-demonstrated and R7 FRESH was unsatisfiable after any edit to the driver. The gap surfaced when scripts/rust_frontend.sh was fixed for GNU hosts: both its mktemp calls used the BSD `-t <prefix>` spelling, which GNU coreutils reads as a TEMPLATE and refuses, so the driver exited 2 before doing any work and local_gate.sh full mode was unrunnable on this clone. A driver that cannot RUN reports no violations, which is indistinguishable from a clean tree -- this arm makes that indistinguishable state impossible to fake by planting a formatting violation and requiring the driver to NAME the offending file.
